examples.ko: 당분이 많은 음료는 이를 상하게 해요.
examples.en: Drinks high in sugar damage your teeth.

examples.ko: 저는 당분을 줄이려고 과일 주스를 안 마셔요.
examples.en: I don't drink fruit juice to cut down on sugar.

examples.ko: 과일에는 당분 함량이 높은 것도 있어요.
examples.en: Some fruits have a high sugar content.

examples.ko: 당분은 운동 전에 에너지를 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: Sugar can give you energy before exercise.

examples.ko: 이 과자는 당분 때문에 너무 달아요.
examples.en: This snack is too sweet because of the sugar.

examples.ko: 당분이 든 간식은 한꺼번에 많이 먹지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't eat a lot of snacks containing sugar at once.

explain: '설탕'은 요리에 넣는 하얀 가루이고, '당분'은 음식 속에 든 단 성분이에요. 그래서 '설탕을 넣다'는 되지만 '당분을 넣다'는 어색해요. 건강 이야기에서 '당분을 줄이다'를 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: This bread is low in sugar, so it's healthy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 속 단 성분이 적다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a food has little sugar content.

phrases.example: 운동 후에는 당분을 섭취하는 게 좋아요.
phrases.en: It's good to take in some sugar after exercise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹어서 몸에 들어오게 한다는 말이에요. 건강 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means taking sugar into the body by eating. Used in health talk.

phrases.en: Fruit also contains sugar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 안에 단 성분이 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a food has sugar inside.

explain_en: 설탕 is the white powder you add when cooking, while 당분 is the sweet component inside food. So 설탕을 넣다 works, but 당분을 넣다 sounds odd. In health talk, 당분을 줄이다 is common.

examples.ko: 시장에 가면 먹을거리 구경하는 재미가 있어요.
examples.en: Going to the market is fun for looking at all the food.

examples.ko: 소풍 갈 때 먹을거리를 넉넉히 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I packed plenty of food for the picnic.
Seoul has plenty of both sights and food.
Food booths are lined up at the festival.

examples.ko: 먹을거리는 제가 준비할 테니 음료만 사 오세요.
examples.en: I'll prepare the food, so just bring drinks.
These days people care a lot about safe food.

explain: '음식'보다 '먹을 수 있는 것들'이라는 느낌이 강해서 시장, 축제, 여행 이야기에 잘 어울려요. '먹거리'도 표준어로 같이 써요. '볼거리', '즐길 거리'와 짝을 이뤄 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: There is a lot of food at the festival.
phrases.nuance_ko: '먹을거리'와 같은 뜻의 표준어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A standard word with the same meaning as '먹을거리'.

phrases.en: This neighborhood has lots of food to eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹을 것이 많은 곳을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe a place with plenty to eat.

phrases.en: Travel spots have lots to see and lots to eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '볼거리'와 짝을 이뤄 여행이나 축제를 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with '볼거리' when talking about trips and festivals.

explain_en: It feels more like 'things to eat' than '음식', so it suits talk about markets, festivals and trips. '먹거리' is also a standard word with the same meaning. It often appears in a set with '볼거리' and '즐길 거리'.

examples.en: Noodles made from buckwheat are refreshing.
A buckwheat pillow is easy on the neck.
I ate buckwheat crepes in Gangwon Province.
The buckwheat flower field bloomed white.

examples.ko: 메밀은 쌀이나 밀보다 구수한 맛이 나요.
examples.en: Buckwheat has a nuttier flavor than rice or wheat.
In summer I often eat buckwheat noodles.

explain: 음식으로는 '메밀국수', '메밀묵', '메밀 전병'처럼 이어서 많이 써요. '모밀'이라고 하는 사람도 있지만 표준어는 '메밀'이에요.

phrases.en: In summer I eat cool buckwheat noodles.
phrases.nuance_ko: 메밀로 만든 국수예요. 음식 이름으로 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Noodles made from buckwheat, the most common food name using this word.

phrases.en: My grandmother made seasoned buckwheat jelly for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 메밀 가루로 굳혀 만든 묵이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A jelly set from buckwheat flour.

phrases.en: The buckwheat flowers bloomed white in autumn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 아니라 식물의 꽃을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the flower of the plant rather than food.

explain_en: In food it is often part of compounds such as 메밀국수, 메밀묵 and 메밀 전병. Some people say 모밀, but the standard form is 메밀.

examples.en: Rice for meals is usually made with regular non-glutinous rice.

examples.ko: 떡은 멥쌀과 찹쌀 중에 뭘로 만들어요?
examples.en: Is rice cake made from non-glutinous or glutinous rice?
Non-glutinous rice is less sticky than glutinous rice.
Garaetteok is made with non-glutinous rice flour.
I bought a bag of non-glutinous rice at the mart.

examples.ko: 멥쌀에 찹쌀을 조금 섞으면 밥이 더 쫀득해요.
examples.en: If you mix a little glutinous rice into non-glutinous rice, the rice gets chewier.

explain: 찹쌀의 반대말로, 우리가 평소 밥으로 먹는 쌀이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '쌀'이라고 하고, 떡이나 요리법에서 찹쌀과 구분할 때 '멥쌀'을 써요. 가루로 만든 것은 '멥쌀가루'라고 해요.

phrases.en: We make garaetteok with nonglutinous rice flour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멥쌀을 가루로 만든 것으로, 떡 만들 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Rice flour made from nonglutinous rice, often seen in rice cake recipes.

phrases.en: I mixed nonglutinous and glutinous rice to make rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 쌀을 같이 말할 때 짝으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about the two kinds of rice together.
phrases.en_equiv: to mix the two kinds of rice

phrases.example: 멥쌀로 떡을 만들면 찹쌀보다 덜 끈적해요.
phrases.en: Rice cakes made from nonglutinous rice are less sticky than those made from glutinous rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '로'를 붙여 재료로 쓴다고 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '로' shows it is used as an ingredient.
phrases.en_equiv: to make rice cake with it

explain_en: It is the opposite of '찹쌀' (glutinous rice) and is the rice eaten as everyday meals. In daily talk people just say '쌀', and use '멥쌀' when distinguishing it from glutinous rice in rice cake or recipes. The flour is called '멥쌀가루'.

en: side dish made for long storage

examples.ko: 일요일마다 한 주 동안 먹을 밑반찬을 만들어요.
examples.en: Every Sunday I make side dishes to eat for the week.

examples.ko: 엄마가 밑반찬과 과일을 잔뜩 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: Mom sent me lots of side dishes and fruit.
Stir-fried anchovies are a typical make-ahead side dish.

examples.ko: 밑반찬이 있으니까 바쁜 날에도 밥 먹기 편해요.
examples.en: With make-ahead side dishes, meals are easy even on busy days.

examples.ko: 밑반찬도 직접 만든다고 해서 믿고 먹어요.
examples.en: They make even the side dishes themselves, so I eat them with confidence.

examples.ko: 밑반찬은 냉장고에 넣어 두면 오래 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you keep make-ahead side dishes in the fridge, you can eat them for a long time.

explain: 멸치볶음이나 장조림처럼 한 번 만들어 두고 두고두고 먹는 반찬을 말해요. 식당에서 나오는 기본 반찬은 보통 그냥 '반찬'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: It's convenient if you make side dishes ahead on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 두고 먹을 반찬을 미리 준비한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means preparing side dishes ahead to eat for a while.

phrases.en: My grandmother sent side dishes by parcel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족이 멀리 있는 사람에게 반찬을 보낼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when family sends food to someone far away.

phrases.en: I stopped by a side dish shop on my way home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반찬을 사서 먹을 수 있는 가게를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shop where you can buy side dishes.

explain_en: It refers to side dishes like stir-fried anchovies or braised beef in soy sauce that you make once and eat over many days. The basic side dishes at a restaurant are usually just called '반찬'.

examples.en: In summer I eat oiji soaked in water.
Grandmother made the oiji herself.
Seasoned oiji is a good side dish for rice.
There is still some oiji left in the fridge.
I sliced the oiji thinly and rinsed it in water.

examples.ko: 입맛 없을 때 오이지에 찬물을 부어 먹어요.
examples.en: When I have no appetite, I pour cold water over oiji and eat it.

explain: 오이를 짭짤하게 절인 반찬이라 보통 썰어서 물에 헹궈 무침으로 먹거나 찬물에 담가 먹어요. 여름 밥상에 자주 올라오는 반찬이에요.

phrases.en: Seasoned oiji brings back my appetite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 썰어서 양념에 무친 가장 흔한 먹는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to eat it: sliced and seasoned.

phrases.example: 더운 날에는 오이지 냉국을 시원하게 먹어요.
phrases.en: On hot days, I enjoy cold oiji soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찬물에 담가 먹는 여름 음식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A summer dish served in cold water.

phrases.en: When summer comes, my mom makes oiji.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 직접 만들어 절일 때 '담그다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Damgeuda' is the verb for making pickled foods at home.

explain_en: It is cucumber pickled salty, so it is usually sliced and rinsed, then eaten as a seasoned side dish or soaked in cold water. It is a common side dish on summer tables.

examples.en: Yogurt contains a lot of lactic acid bacteria.
My stomach feels better since I eat probiotics every day.
When kimchi ripens well, lactic acid bacteria form in it.

examples.ko: 약국에서 유산균 제품을 한 상자 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a box of probiotic products at the pharmacy.
I gave my child a probiotic drink.

examples.ko: 유산균이 장에 좋다고 해서 챙겨 먹어요.
examples.en: They say lactic acid bacteria are good for the gut, so I make sure to take them.

explain: 유산균은 요구르트, 김치, 치즈 같은 발효 음식에 들어 있는 균이에요. 광고에서는 '프로바이오틱스'라는 영어 말도 같이 써요. 상한 음식 속 해로운 균은 '식중독균'이라고 해서 구분해요.

phrases.en: My child likes lactic acid bacteria drinks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유산균이 들어 있는 마시는 제품을 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a drinkable product that contains lactic acid bacteria.

phrases.en: This kimchi contains lactic acid bacteria.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식 안에 유산균이 있다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain that a food contains lactic acid bacteria.

phrases.en: I take lactic acid bacteria every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 약으로 유산균을 먹는 습관을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the habit of taking them as food or a supplement.

explain_en: 유산균 is the bacteria found in fermented foods such as yogurt, kimchi and cheese. Ads also use the English word 프로바이오틱스 alongside it. Harmful bacteria in spoiled food are called 식중독균 (food-poisoning bacteria), which keeps the two apart.

examples.en: You add yeast when you make bread.
The bread did not rise because there was no yeast.
Yeast grows well in a warm place.
I mixed a little yeast and sugar into the dough.

examples.ko: 마트에서 이스트 한 봉지만 사 오세요.
examples.en: Please buy just one bag of yeast at the mart.

examples.ko: 반죽에서 이스트 냄새가 조금 나지만 괜찮아요.
examples.en: The dough smells a little of yeast, but it is fine.

explain: 빵과 피자 반죽을 부풀릴 때 넣는 재료예요. 영어 'yeast'에서 온 말이고 '효모'라고도 해요. 집에서 빵을 구울 때는 보통 '이스트'라고 하고, 과학 시간에는 '효모'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: We learned about yeast in science class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이스트와 같은 것을 가리키지만 과학 수업이나 글에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to the same thing as 이스트, but is used more in science classes and writing.

phrases.en: Add one spoonful of yeast to the dough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리법에서 이스트의 양을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase used in recipes to give the amount of yeast.

phrases.en: Bread made with yeast is soft.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이스트를 넣어 부풀린 빵을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe bread that has been leavened with yeast.

explain_en: It is the ingredient that makes bread and pizza dough rise. The word comes from English 'yeast', and the Sino-Korean term is '효모'. At home bakers say '이스트', while science class prefers '효모'.

examples.en: I bought apples and pears at the produce store.

examples.ko: 새벽에 청과물 시장에 가서 물건을 떼어 와요.
examples.en: I go to the produce market at dawn to get goods.
The produce at this supermarket is really fresh.

examples.ko: 요즘 청과물 값이 올라서 장 보기가 부담돼요.
examples.en: Produce prices have gone up, so grocery shopping is a burden.
Mom went to the market to buy fruit and vegetables.

examples.ko: 채소와 과일 같은 청과물은 냉장고에 보관해요.
examples.en: I store produce like vegetables and fruit in the fridge.

explain: 채소와 과일을 한꺼번에 부르는 말이에요. 대화에서는 '과일 가게', '채소 가게'라고 하는 때가 많고, 간판에서는 '○○청과'처럼 보일 때가 있어요.

phrases.en: This shop sells fresh produce.
phrases.nuance_ko: 채소와 과일이 싱싱하다는 뜻으로 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes produce as fresh.

phrases.en: My grandmother sells produce at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 채소와 과일을 판매한다는 뜻의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual pairing for selling fruits and vegetables.

phrases.en: I picked out tangerines at the produce section of the mart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마트에서 채소와 과일을 모아 둔 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The area in a supermarket for fruits and vegetables.

explain_en: It is a single word covering both vegetables and fruit. In conversation people often say '과일 가게' or '채소 가게', and on shop signs you may see names like '○○청과'.

examples.en: I bought a bag of taro at the market.

examples.ko: 토란은 껍질을 벗길 때 손이 가려울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Your hands can get itchy when you peel taro.
We boil taro and put it into soup.

examples.ko: 엄마가 토란과 소고기를 넣고 국을 끓이셨어요.
examples.en: Mom made soup with taro and beef.

examples.ko: 토란 잎에 물방울이 동글동글 맺혀 있어요.
examples.en: Round water drops are beading on the taro leaf.
This shop sells fried taro too.

explain: 감자나 고구마와 달리 날것으로 먹지 않고 익혀서 먹어요. 껍질을 벗길 때 손이 가려울 수 있어서 장갑을 끼는 사람도 있어요. 한국에서는 '토란국'으로 많이 알려져 있어요.

phrases.en: My mother made taro soup for Chuseok.
phrases.nuance_ko: 토란으로 만든 대표적인 한국 음식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The best-known Korean dish made with taro.

phrases.en: I boiled the taro and peeled it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 토란은 날로 먹지 않고 익혀서 먹어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Taro is cooked before eating, not eaten raw.

phrases.example: 토란 껍질을 벗길 때는 장갑을 껴요.
phrases.en: I wear gloves when I peel taro.
phrases.nuance_ko: 손이 가려울 수 있어서 장갑을 끼는 일이 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: People often wear gloves because it can make hands itch.

explain_en: Unlike potatoes or sweet potatoes, taro is not eaten raw but cooked. Peeling it can make your hands itchy, so some people wear gloves. In Korea it is best known as an ingredient in '토란국' (taro soup).

examples.en: I put a lot of toppings on the pizza.
Which topping is the tastiest?
I'll have chocolate as the ice cream topping.
Adding a topping costs one thousand won.
You can pick the toppings yourself too.
If you add fruit as a topping, it is fresher.

explain: '토핑을 올리다', '토핑을 추가하다'처럼 써요. 한식에서 음식 위에 얹는 것은 '고명'이라고 부르고, 피자나 아이스크림처럼 서양식 음식에는 '토핑'을 써요.

phrases.en: I'm choosing the pizza toppings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주문할 때 원하는 토핑을 정하는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Picking the toppings you want when ordering.

phrases.en: Please leave off the onion topping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹기 싫은 토핑을 빼 달라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask to leave out a topping you don't want.

phrases.en: Extra toppings are 1,000 won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 돈을 더 내고 넣는 토핑을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Toppings you pay extra for at a shop.

explain_en: It pairs with '토핑을 올리다' and '토핑을 추가하다'. What goes on top of Korean dishes is called '고명', while '토핑' is used for things like pizza and ice cream.
